title: The Summit of the Sepik Basin
premise: Beatrix Underhill, a disgraced railroad engineer hiding in the Sepik Basin's port town, carries a map of closed mountain lines and a debt owed to the man who once saved her life. When an earthquake tide exposes a cave said to hold the region's lost colonial gold, Beatrix is dragged into a race against a corrupt mining magnate, her own creditors, and the coming snows. Guided by a local tracker, Ila, whose loyalty she must earn and then betray to survive, Beatrix discovers the 'treasure' is actually evidence of a massacre the magnate's family buried. In the end, Beatrix chooses truth over safety: she detonates the cave entrance, destroying the proof and the fortune alike, and testifies in the lowlands knowing it may cost her everything but finally frees her from her debt.
about_author: Sable Pemberton is the pen name of a former surveyor who spent six years mapping river routes through Papua New Guinea before turning to fiction. Their novels blend engineering precision with a deep suspicion of anyone who claims to own a mountain.

chapters.title: The Tide Takes Something Back
chapters.summary: Beatrix Underhill, POV. Working as a harbor clerk in Wewak, Beatrix watches an earthquake-driven tide drain the bay and expose a cave mouth locals refuse to name. She sketches it out of habit. The emotional beat: restless unease—the first crack in her carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: A Debt Written in Ink
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Collector Ambrose Kell arrives with papers: her debt to financier Marcus Vane is due in sixty days, payable only in something Vane wants more than money—access to the cave. Flashback reveals Vane once pulled her from a collapsed tunnel. Beat: dread mixed with old gratitude.

chapters.title: The Map of Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. She studies her father's map of abandoned mountain rail grades—the only viable route over the range before snowfall. A stranger, Ila, catches her tracing it and offers to guide her for reasons he won't explain. Beat: wary alliance formed out of mutual need.

chapters.title: Legends Charge Admission
chapters.summary: Ila, POV. Ila explains the cave's legend: the gold of the Halvorsen expedition, which vanished in 1911 along with forty porters. He believes his grandfather was among them. He'll guide Beatrix if she promises the dead get named. Beat: grief disguised as bargaining.

chapters.title: Vane's Offer
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Vane makes it explicit: bring back what's in the cave and the debt dies; fail and he takes her engineer's license and her freedom. He assigns his enforcer, Dray, to accompany her. Beat: the trap closes with a smile.

chapters.title: Provisions and Lies
chapters.summary: Dray, POV. Dray stocks the expedition, secretly reporting to Vane that Beatrix seems to know more about the route than she admits. Beatrix lies smoothly about the map's condition. Beat: cat-and-mouse begins; trust is currency neither can afford.

chapters.title: Into the Green Silence
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. The party of five enters the basin interior—river crossings, leeches, heat. Ila reads the land like text while Dray blunders. First night, someone searches Beatrix's pack. Beat: the wilderness strips away pretense.

chapters.title: The Washed-Out Grade
chapters.summary: Ila, POV. They reach the first closed rail line, a miracle of cut stone swallowed by jungle. Beatrix reads the engineering aloud, and Ila sees her differently—not a debtor but a builder. Beat: grudging respect kindles.

chapters.title: River of Small Bones
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. A porter finds bones in a gravel bar—expedition-era, decades old. Dray wants to move on; Ila refuses until they're marked. The party fractures along moral lines. Beat: loyalty vs. truth takes its first casualty.

chapters.title: Storm on the Shoulder
chapters.summary: Ila, POV. A storm forces them onto a cliff shelf; a porter falls and survives barely. Dray 'accidentally' lets supplies burn, making return impossible and forward the only option. Beat: rage and realization—they are prisoners now.

chapters.title: What Beatrix Buried
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Around the fire, she confesses: the collapse Vane saved her from was caused by her own falsified load calculations, covered up by him ever since. Her debt is blackmail wearing a ledger's clothes. Beat: shame transformed into resolve.

chapters.title: The Snowline
chapters.summary: Dray, POV. They cross the snowline early—winter ahead of schedule. Dray radios Vane and learns the truth: there is no debt forgiveness. Vane wants witnesses silenced. Dray hesitates for the first time. Beat: the enforcer's mask slips.

chapters.title: Cave of the Forty Names
chapters.summary: Ila, POV. They find the cave's upper entrance and inside, not gold but records: ledgers, photographs, and a mass grave—the Halvorsen party murdered by the company that became Vane's empire. Ila finds his grandfather's name. Beat: sacred fury.

chapters.title: Gold in the Dark
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Deeper chambers do hold bullion—and dynamite stores left by the original company. Dray orders everyone sealed in while he signals Vane's helicopter. Beatrix realizes Vane never intended survivors. Beat: cold terror sharpening into calculation.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Ila, POV. Ila leads an escape through flooded lower galleries using Beatrix's knowledge of the mine's drainage design. One porter drowns saving the records. Beat: sacrifice; the cost of carrying truth becomes literal weight.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Tree Line
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Above ground, Dray corners them—but instead of shooting, he hands over his radio and confesses Vane ordered the deaths of the last people who found this place. He asks to be left behind as penance. Beat: unexpected mercy from an unlikely source.

chapters.title: Race Before the White Silence
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Three remain, racing down the closed rail grade as the storm front hits. Beatrix engineers their descent—trestle crossings, a handcar on rotted rails—in a whiteout. Beat: her craft, long a source of guilt, becomes salvation.

chapters.title: Vane at the Mouth
chapters.summary: Ila, POV. They emerge at the coast to find Vane waiting with men and lawyers. He offers Beatrix full pardon and wealth if the records burn tonight. Ila watches her weigh survival against the forty names. Beat: the thematic fulcrum—loyalty vs. truth made flesh.

chapters.title: The Charge
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Beatrix agrees—then uses her engineer's timing to fire the dynamite stores, collapsing the cave, the gold, and Vane's leverage in one blast. The shockwave buries the massacre's evidence forever, but the copies survive in Ila's oilskin. Beat: explosive climax; destruction as testimony.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. In the lowlands courthouse, Beatrix testifies, surrendering her license and admitting her old crime fully. Vane's empire cracks under the records' weight. She loses everything she spent the book protecting. Beat: bitter, cleansing honesty.

chapters.title: Forty Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Ila, POV. At a memorial in his village, Ila reads the recovered names of the dead. Beatrix stands at the edge, uninvited but not turned away. Ila gives her his grandfather's compass. Beat: mourning becoming belonging.

chapters.title: Open Lines
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Months later, Beatrix works rebuilding a mountain rail line—honestly this time—as a hired hand, debt-free and anonymous by choice rather than fear. A letter arrives: the government wants her to survey new lines into the highlands. She says yes. Beat: quiet hope; the price paid has bought a real beginning.
